name: Jayden Mills
presenting_complaint: Sudden severe left testicular pain for 3 hours

medical_history.social: Year 11 student. Lives with parents. Non-smoker. Pain woke him from sleep.

validation_criteria.presenting_scenario: Jayden Mills, a 16-year-old boy, presents with sudden-onset severe left testicular pain that woke him from sleep 3 hours ago, associated with nausea and one episode of vomiting. He is in obvious distress. HR 104. The left hemiscrotum is swollen and exquisitely tender with a high-riding testis and an absent cremasteric reflex.
validation_criteria.task: Document your assessment and initial management as the admitting RMO.

subjective: Sudden-onset severe unilateral testicular pain, time of onset documented precisely (6-hour window to salvage)
Associated nausea and vomiting (typical of torsion), preceding trauma or exertion, prior similar self-resolving episodes (intermittent torsion)
Absence of urinary symptoms (dysuria/frequency more suggestive of epididymo-orchitis), sexual history where appropriate
SOCRATES of pain and any radiation to lower abdomen/groin
Screen for abdominal pain (torsion can present as lower abdominal pain), fever
objective: Scrotal exam: high-riding, horizontal-lying testis, swollen exquisitely tender hemiscrotum, absent cremasteric reflex
Negative Prehn's sign (elevation does not relieve pain) supporting torsion over epididymitis
Assess for other causes: torsion of appendix testis (blue-dot sign), hernia, cellulitis, trauma
Vital signs and pain score; urinalysis to help assess for infection
Do NOT delay definitive management to obtain a Doppler ultrasound - clinical diagnosis mandates theatre
assessment: Testicular torsion until proven otherwise (sudden pain, high-riding testis, absent cremasteric reflex, vomiting)
Surgical emergency - 6-hour window from onset to preserve testicular viability documented
Differential: torsion of appendix testis, epididymo-orchitis, incarcerated inguinal hernia, trauma/haematocele
plan: Call urology/surgical registrar IMMEDIATELY - before and independent of ordering any ultrasound
Nil by mouth from now, IV access, group and hold, consent for scrotal exploration
IV analgesia titrated (e.g. fentanyl 25-50 microg IV or morphine 2.5-5mg IV) and antiemetic (ondansetron 4mg IV)
Urgent scrotal exploration and bilateral orchidopexy (fixation of contralateral testis); orchidectomy if non-viable
A negative or equivocal Doppler ultrasound does NOT exclude torsion - do not let it delay theatre
Document onset-to-presentation time and escalate for emergency operating theatre now

critical_errors: Waiting for a Doppler ultrasound before calling urology / delaying surgical exploration - a negative ultrasound does not exclude torsion and the delay costs the testis
Misdiagnosing as epididymo-orchitis and treating with antibiotics instead of urgent surgical exploration
Failing to call urology and organise emergency theatre within the 6-hour salvage window
must_not_miss: Testicular torsion treated as time-critical surgical emergency
Immediate urology referral without waiting for imaging
